lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.27 - A Listen and say. Then practise.

details: Listen and say checks understanding of word meaning and pronunciation of the zoo animals. Then  practise allows students to repeat given words in a structured question and answer.
Look for careful listening and correct pronunciation of each animal, correct production of the grammar structure, particularly the ‘s’ of the contracted ‘What’s’ and ‘it’s’, and authentic intonation.
“Today we’re at the zoo! I’m so excited to see all the animals. Can you help me learn their names?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.27 - B. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer gives students controlled practice using the target language to ask and respond to simple questions, in this case the plural demonstrative pronoun ‘those’.

Look for correct formation of the question form, particularly the long /əʊ/ sound in ‘those’, correct pronunciation of ‘they’re’ and the plural form in the answer, Encourage authentic intonation in both the question and the answer.
“Look, there’s our friends Amy and Nick! They look confused. Let’s see if we can help them.”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.81 - A Look and number

details: Look and number consolidates recognition of the written word and word-concept association.
Look for understanding of the words through students’ correct choices and neat number writing in students’ books.
“Amy and Nick need our help remembering  the names of all the animals.  Look! Here are some clues! Let’s connect the words to the pictures!”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.81 - B Connect and write

details: Connect and write gives students the opportunity to produce the words in written form, whilst consolidating the concept.
Look for correct identification of each animal, correct spelling and neat handwriting between the lines.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.28 - Speaking Memory game

details: The memory game provides freer oral production practice of the grammar structure, further consolidating the singular-plural distinction between ‘that’ and ‘those’. It also consolidates the association between the spoken words and the concepts (zoo animals).

Look for correct verb forms (‘is’ with the singular ‘that’ and ‘are’ with the plural ‘those’), correct pronunciation and authentic intonation, correct identification of the animals in singular and plural form.
“We had so much fun at the zoo! Let’s play a game to help us remember all the animals we saw.”
